tagline: Inspect, read, and safely plan typed Google Search Console operations.

source_cli.name: Google Search Console API
source_cli.reference: Official REST discovery documents for Search Console v3 and searchconsole v1

global_flags.name: credential
global_flags.summary: Credential name to use for the Google Search Console request.

global_flags.name: limit
global_flags.summary: Maximum PM ETL records to emit; does not control Search Console rowLimit.

global_flags.name: max-bytes
global_flags.summary: Maximum direct-read response bytes; typed operations are capped at 16 MiB and each Google Search Console operation declares a lower limit.

global_flags.name: plan
global_flags.summary: Execute an approved reverse-ETL plan by id.

global_flags.name: preview
global_flags.summary: Preview a reverse-ETL write command without making a network mutation.

global_flags.name: approve
global_flags.summary: Approval token required to execute a reverse-ETL plan.

global_flags.name: confirm
global_flags.summary: Typed confirmation challenge for destructive reverse-ETL writes.

flags.summary: Search Console site property URL or sc-domain property.

commands.risk: medium: adds a site property to the authenticated Search Console account; requires reverse ETL plan and approval
commands.approval: Use reverse ETL plan -> preview -> approval -> execute. No raw HTTP body is accepted; the record must match writes.json.

commands.summary: Plan deleting a Search Console site property through destructive reverse ETL.

flags.name: site-url
flags.summary: Search Console site property URL or sc-domain property.

commands.risk: high: removes a site property from the authenticated Search Console account; requires reverse ETL plan, approval, and destructive confirmation
commands.approval: Use reverse ETL plan -> preview -> approval -> typed destructive confirmation -> execute. Missing provider records are idempotent for HTTP 404.

help_topics.name: parity
help_topics.summary: Official Search Console parity in this bundle covers 11 operations: 4 ETL read endpoint groups, 4 reverse-ETL write actions, and 3 typed bounded direct reads. There are no generic raw HTTP, body, query, binary, or CDC escape hatches.
